questions.question: What is Vue.js?
questions.answer: Vue.js is a progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces. Combines HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in single-file components. Reactive and easy to learn.

questions.question: What is the difference between Vue 2 and Vue 3?
questions.answer: Vue 3 uses Composition API (optional), Vue 2 uses Options API. Vue 3 has better TypeScript support, smaller bundle size, and improved performance.

questions.question: What is data binding in Vue?
questions.answer: Data binding connects component data to template. Two-way binding with v-model, one-way with {{ }}. Automatically updates when data changes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of v-if and v-show?
questions.answer: v-if conditionally renders element (removes from DOM), v-show toggles display CSS. v-if is better for infrequent toggles, v-show for frequent toggles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of v-for?
questions.answer: v-for renders list of items. Syntax: v-for='item in items'. Can use index: v-for='(item, index) in items'. Always use :key for tracking.

questions.question: What is the purpose of v-on?
questions.answer: v-on binds event listeners. Syntax: v-on:click='method' or @click='method'. Can pass arguments and use modifiers like .prevent, .stop.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'data' property?
questions.answer: data returns object with reactive properties. Must be a function. Properties become reactive and trigger re-renders when changed.

questions.question: What are computed properties?
questions.answer: Computed properties are derived from data, cached based on dependencies. Syntax: computed: { fullName() { return this.first + this.last } }. Better than methods for caching.

questions.question: What are watchers in Vue?
questions.answer: Watchers observe data changes and execute callbacks. Syntax: watch: { message(newVal, oldVal) {} }. Useful for side effects and async operations.

questions.question: What are Vue lifecycle hooks?
questions.answer: Lifecycle hooks execute at specific stages. created, mounted, updated, destroyed. Composition API uses onMounted, onUpdated, etc.

questions.question: What are Vue components?
questions.answer: Components are reusable Vue instances. Can be single-file (.vue) or object-based. Enable modularity and code reuse.

questions.question: What are props in Vue?
questions.answer: Props pass data from parent to child. Read-only, child cannot modify. Syntax: props: ['message'] or props: { message: String }.

questions.question: What is event emission in Vue?
questions.answer: Child emits events to parent with $emit(). Parent listens with v-on or @. Enables child-to-parent communication.

questions.question: What are slots in Vue?
questions.answer: Slots allow parent to pass content to child. Named slots for multiple content areas. Enables flexible component composition.

questions.question: What is v-bind?
questions.answer: v-bind binds data to HTML attributes. Syntax: v-bind:href='url' or :href='url'. Enables dynamic attribute values.

questions.question: What is v-model?
questions.answer: v-model creates two-way binding. Syntax: v-model='message'. Combines v-bind and v-on. Works with input, textarea, select.

questions.question: What are filters in Vue?
questions.answer: Filters format text output. Syntax: {{ message | capitalize }}. Can chain filters. Vue 3 recommends methods or computed properties instead.

questions.question: What are mixins in Vue?
questions.answer: Mixins share reusable logic between components. Merge with component options. Can have data, methods, lifecycle hooks.

questions.question: What is the Composition API?
questions.answer: Composition API organizes code by feature instead of type. Uses setup() function. Better for large components and code reuse.

questions.question: What is reactivity in Vue?
questions.answer: Reactivity automatically updates DOM when data changes. Vue tracks dependencies and triggers re-renders. Use ref() and reactive() in Composition API.

questions.question: What is v-class?
questions.answer: v-class is not a directive. Use :class or v-bind:class. Syntax: :class='{ active: isActive }' or :class='[activeClass, errorClass]'.

questions.question: What is v-style?
questions.answer: v-style is not a directive. Use :style or v-bind:style. Syntax: :style='{ color: activeColor, fontSize: fontSize + "px" }'.

questions.question: What are transitions in Vue?
questions.answer: Transitions add animations when elements enter/leave. Use <transition> component. Provides CSS classes for animation hooks.

questions.question: What are animations in Vue?
questions.answer: Animations apply CSS animations to elements. Use <transition> with animation classes. Different from transitions (discrete vs continuous).

questions.question: What is Vue Router?
questions.answer: Vue Router enables single-page application routing. Maps URLs to components. Provides navigation and lazy loading.

questions.question: What is Vuex?
questions.answer: Vuex is state management library for Vue. Centralized store with state, mutations, actions, getters. Better than prop drilling for large apps.

questions.question: What is v-text?
questions.answer: v-text sets element's text content. Syntax: v-text='message'. Similar to {{ message }} but lower priority.

questions.question: What is v-html?
questions.answer: v-html sets element's HTML content. Syntax: v-html='htmlString'. Dangerous with user input (XSS risk). Use only with trusted content.

questions.question: What are methods in Vue?
questions.answer: Methods are functions in component. Syntax: methods: { handleClick() {} }. Called with events or manually. Not cached like computed properties.

questions.question: What are custom directives?
questions.answer: Custom directives extend Vue functionality. Syntax: directive('focus', { mounted(el) { el.focus() } }). Useful for DOM manipulation.

questions.question: What is a single-file component?
questions.answer: Single-file component (.vue) contains template, script, and style. Enables scoped CSS and better organization. Requires build step.

questions.question: What is the setup() function?
questions.answer: setup() is entry point for Composition API. Receives props and context. Returns object with reactive data and methods.

questions.question: What is ref() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: ref() creates reactive reference. Syntax: const count = ref(0). Access with count.value. Automatically unwrapped in templates.

questions.question: What is reactive() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: reactive() creates reactive object. Syntax: const state = reactive({ count: 0 }). No .value needed. Better for objects.

questions.question: What is a composable in Vue 3?
questions.answer: Composable is reusable function using Composition API. Returns reactive data and methods. Similar to mixins but more flexible.

questions.question: What is v-cloak?
questions.answer: v-cloak hides uncompiled template. Removed after Vue compiles. Prevents {{ }} from showing before Vue initializes.

questions.question: What are event modifiers?
questions.answer: Event modifiers modify event behavior. Examples: .prevent (preventDefault), .stop (stopPropagation), .once (one-time), .self (only direct target).

questions.question: What are key modifiers?
questions.answer: Key modifiers filter keyboard events. Examples: .enter, .tab, .esc, .space. Syntax: @keyup.enter='submit'.

questions.question: What are system modifiers?
questions.answer: System modifiers check modifier keys. Examples: .ctrl, .shift, .alt, .meta. Syntax: @click.ctrl='handleCtrlClick'.

questions.question: What is v-once?
questions.answer: v-once renders element once and skips updates. Useful for static content. Improves performance for unchanging data.

questions.question: What is component registration?
questions.answer: Components can be global (app.component()) or local (components: {}). Global available everywhere, local only in parent component.

questions.question: What is v-pre?
questions.answer: v-pre skips compilation for element. Useful for displaying template syntax. Improves performance for static content.

questions.question: What are async components?
questions.answer: Async components load on demand. Syntax: defineAsyncComponent(() => import('./Component.vue')). Useful for code splitting and lazy loading.

questions.question: What is Suspense in Vue 3?
questions.answer: Suspense handles async components. Shows fallback while loading. Syntax: <Suspense><Component /></Suspense>.

questions.question: What is Teleport in Vue 3?
questions.answer: Teleport renders component in different DOM location. Useful for modals, tooltips. Syntax: <Teleport to='body'><Modal /></Teleport>.

questions.question: What is the virtual DOM?
questions.answer: Virtual DOM is in-memory representation of DOM. Vue updates virtual DOM first, then syncs with real DOM. Improves performance.

questions.question: What is key in v-for?
questions.answer: :key helps Vue identify elements. Improves performance and prevents state issues. Use unique identifier, not index for dynamic lists.

questions.question: What is v-slot?
questions.answer: v-slot defines slot content. Syntax: <template v-slot:header>Content</template>. Shorthand: #header. Enables named slots.

questions.question: What is provide/inject?
questions.answer: provide/inject passes data through component tree without props. Syntax: provide('key', value) and inject('key'). Useful for deeply nested components.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-if and v-for priority?
questions.answer: v-if has higher priority than v-for. Avoid using together. If needed, wrap v-if in separate element or use computed property.

questions.question: What is the .sync modifier?
questions.answer: .sync enables two-way binding for props. Vue 2 feature. Vue 3 uses v-model instead. Syntax: :title.sync='title'.

questions.question: What is watchEffect() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: watchEffect() automatically tracks dependencies. Syntax: watchEffect(() => { console.log(count.value) }). Simpler than watch() for simple cases.

questions.question: What is computed() in Composition API?
questions.answer: computed() creates computed property in Composition API. Syntax: const fullName = computed(() => first.value + last.value). Returns ref.

questions.question: What is the el property in Vue?
questions.answer: el specifies DOM element to mount Vue instance. Syntax: el: '#app'. Vue replaces element with component. Not used in Composition API.

questions.question: What is v-for with object?
questions.answer: v-for iterates over object properties. Syntax: v-for='(value, key) in object'. Can also get index: v-for='(value, key, index) in object'.

questions.question: What is v-for with range?
questions.answer: v-for can iterate over number range. Syntax: v-for='n in 10'. Creates array [1,2,3...10]. Useful for pagination or repetition.

questions.question: What is component scope?
questions.answer: Each component has isolated scope. Data, methods, computed properties are local. Props and events enable communication.

questions.question: What is the difference between component and element?
questions.answer: Component is Vue instance with template/script/style, element is HTML tag. Components are reusable, elements are built-in.

questions.question: What is dynamic component?
questions.answer: Dynamic component switches between components. Syntax: <component :is='currentComponent' />. Useful for tabs or conditional rendering.

questions.question: What is onMounted() in Composition API?
questions.answer: onMounted() runs after component mounts. Syntax: onMounted(() => { /* setup */ }). Replaces mounted() hook from Options API.

questions.question: What is scoped CSS in Vue?
questions.answer: Scoped CSS limits styles to component. Syntax: <style scoped>. Vue adds unique attributes to elements. Prevents style conflicts.

questions.question: What is the difference between template and render function?
questions.answer: Template is HTML-like syntax, render function returns VNode. Template is simpler, render function is more flexible.

questions.question: What is onBeforeMount() in Composition API?
questions.answer: onBeforeMount() runs before component mounts. Syntax: onBeforeMount(() => { /* setup */ }). Replaces beforeMount() hook.

questions.question: What is the difference between :class and v-bind:class?
questions.answer: :class is shorthand for v-bind:class. Both do the same thing. :class is preferred for brevity.

questions.question: What is onUpdated() in Composition API?
questions.answer: onUpdated() runs after component updates. Syntax: onUpdated(() => { /* cleanup */ }). Replaces updated() hook.

questions.question: What is the difference between :style and v-bind:style?
questions.answer: :style is shorthand for v-bind:style. Both do the same thing. :style is preferred for brevity.

questions.question: What is onBeforeUnmount() in Composition API?
questions.answer: onBeforeUnmount() runs before component unmounts. Syntax: onBeforeUnmount(() => { /* cleanup */ }). Replaces beforeDestroy() hook.

questions.question: What is the difference between @click and v-on:click?
questions.answer: @click is shorthand for v-on:click. Both do the same thing. @click is preferred for brevity.

questions.question: What is onUnmounted() in Composition API?
questions.answer: onUnmounted() runs after component unmounts. Syntax: onUnmounted(() => { /* cleanup */ }). Replaces destroyed() hook.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-bind and :?
questions.answer: v-bind is full syntax, : is shorthand. Both bind data to attributes. : is preferred for brevity.

questions.question: What is computed with getter and setter?
questions.answer: Computed can have get and set. Syntax: computed({ get: () => {}, set: (val) => {} }). Enables two-way computed properties.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-model and :value?
questions.answer: v-model is two-way binding, :value is one-way. v-model combines :value and @input. v-model is simpler for forms.

questions.question: What is shallowRef() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: shallowRef() creates shallow reactive reference. Only top-level reactivity. Better performance for large objects.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-on and @?
questions.answer: v-on is full syntax, @ is shorthand. Both bind event listeners. @ is preferred for brevity.

questions.question: What is shallowReactive() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: shallowReactive() creates shallow reactive object. Only top-level reactivity. Better performance for large objects.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-model and .sync?
questions.answer: v-model is standard two-way binding, .sync is for props. Vue 3 uses v-model instead of .sync. v-model is preferred.

questions.question: What is readonly() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: readonly() creates read-only reactive object. Prevents modifications. Useful for preventing accidental mutations.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-show and v-if?
questions.answer: v-show toggles display CSS (stays in DOM), v-if removes from DOM. v-show is better for frequent toggles, v-if for infrequent.

questions.question: What is isRef() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: isRef() checks if value is ref. Syntax: isRef(value). Returns boolean. Useful for type checking in composables.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and map()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, map() transforms array in JavaScript. v-for is for rendering, map() for data transformation.

questions.question: What is unref() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: unref() unwraps ref if it is one, otherwise returns value. Syntax: unref(value). Useful in composables for handling both refs and values.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and forEach()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, forEach() iterates in JavaScript. v-for is for rendering, forEach() for side effects.

questions.question: What is isReactive() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: isReactive() checks if value is reactive object. Syntax: isReactive(value). Returns boolean. Useful for type checking.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and filter()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, filter() creates filtered array. v-for is for rendering, filter() for data transformation.

questions.question: What is isReadonly() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: isReadonly() checks if value is readonly. Syntax: isReadonly(value). Returns boolean. Useful for type checking.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and reduce()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, reduce() accumulates value. v-for is for rendering, reduce() for aggregation.

questions.question: What is toRef() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: toRef() converts reactive property to ref. Syntax: toRef(object, 'property'). Useful for destructuring reactive objects.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and find()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, find() returns first matching element. v-for is for rendering, find() for searching.

questions.question: What is toRefs() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: toRefs() converts reactive object to refs. Syntax: toRefs(object). Enables destructuring without losing reactivity.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and some()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, some() checks if any element matches. v-for is for rendering, some() for checking.

questions.question: What is toValue() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: toValue() unwraps value (ref or function). Syntax: toValue(value). Handles both refs and functions.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and every()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, every() checks if all elements match. v-for is for rendering, every() for checking.

questions.question: What is markRaw() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: markRaw() marks object as non-reactive. Syntax: markRaw(object). Improves performance for non-reactive data.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and includes()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, includes() checks if element exists. v-for is for rendering, includes() for searching.

questions.question: What is triggerRef() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: triggerRef() manually triggers ref update. Syntax: triggerRef(ref). Useful after mutating non-reactive data.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and indexOf()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, indexOf() finds element position. v-for is for rendering, indexOf() for searching.

questions.question: What is effectScope() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: effectScope() creates scope for reactive effects. Syntax: const scope = effectScope(). Enables batch cleanup of effects.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and lastIndexOf()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, lastIndexOf() finds last element position. v-for is for rendering, lastIndexOf() for searching.

questions.question: What is getCurrentInstance() in Vue 3?
questions.answer: getCurrentInstance() gets current component instance. Syntax: const instance = getCurrentInstance(). Use only in setup() or lifecycle hooks.

questions.question: What is the difference between v-for and join()?
questions.answer: v-for renders list in template, join() combines array into string. v-for is for rendering, join() for string conversion.
